clue.text: Come to blows with reserve-may well be given a pasting!

definitions.text: may well be given a pasting

parts.note: to come to blows is to fight, to have a scrap
to reserve a table is to book it

explanation.surface: Someone spoiling for a fight with a shy person can expect a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pasting' reads as a thrashing, but the definition is literal: cuttings are glued into this album.
explanation.definitionFit: An album of cuttings has items glued onto its pages, so it is regularly pasted into.

clue.text: A pirate shanty with ribald-sounding beginning

indicators.note: beginning puts the sound-alike piece at the front of the answer
ribald-sounding asks for a sound-alike of a word meaning ribald

parts.note: ribald jokes are coarse ones
a sea shanty is a song, an air

explanation.surface: A sea robber's song opens with something rather rude.
explanation.walkthrough: CORS is said like COARSE, which is what ribald means.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or sea raider, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: An Italian writer can be somewhat slow

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An author from Italy may be a little sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical tempo marking means at a moderate walking pace, fairly slow.

clue.text: Wanted to start a new life, as all but ruined

definitions.text: Wanted to start a new life

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of as all but are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a fresh start because nearly everything has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but' looks like 'nearly', but it is simply fodder. The definition plays on an early embryo, the stage at which a new life starts.
explanation.definitionFit: This hollow ball of cells is an early embryo stage, so it is needed to begin an organism.

clue.text: Operating controls for week-end viewing

indicators.note: week-end points to the end letter of the word week

parts.note: eying something is viewing it

explanation.surface: Working the remote for some weekend television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Week-end' reads as Saturday and Sunday; it is the last letter of 'week'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keying is pressing keys, working the buttons of a keyboard or panel.

clue.text: White woolly bloomers!

parts.note: reads as warm pale underwear, but means an Alpine flower with white felted petals

explanation.surface: A pair of pale knitted knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine plant has flowers covered in white woolly hairs, so it is a woolly white bloom.

clue.text: In the US, it's plain

parts.note: reads as something obvious to Americans, but plain is the flat grassland noun

explanation.surface: Americans find it perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The grassy plains of North America are known by this name.

clue.text: Genial characters in debt set straight again

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for debt

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt

indicators.note: the characters of genial are its letters, taken in a new order

explanation.surface: A friendly sort who is overdrawn gets back on track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In debt' is split: 'in' puts EALIGN (the letters of GENIAL rearranged) inside RED, the colour of debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring back into line, to straighten once more.

clue.text: Object, having dreadfully sore back

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters of sore are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone protests because their back is terribly painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the sore body, but it is the definition, as in backing a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate is to support or approve them.

clue.text: Little Greek served with a double is not hurried

parts.note: Gr is the short form of Greek
dual means twofold, double

explanation.surface: A small Greek man given a double measure takes his time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gradual happens slowly, by degrees.

clue.text: Bill the invalid, causing bad feeling

parts.note: an invalid is ill
Will and Bill are both short for William

explanation.surface: Bill, who is laid up sick, is the cause of resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity or hostility towards someone is spite felt against them.

clue.text: Kind of pink vehicle folk will go for

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a nation is a people, a folk

explanation.surface: People are drawn to a vehicle in a particular shade of pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' suggests a colour; here it is the garden flower of the dianthus family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are dianthus flowers, and the familiar buttonhole bloom is one species of them.

clue.text: They'll get into a row for their sporting activity

definitions.text: They'll get into a row for their sporting activity

parts.words: They'll get into a row for their sporting activity
parts.note: reads as people quarrelling over sport, but row rhymes with go: they propel a boat

explanation.surface: Athletes who start arguments about their game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers sit in a boat and row it in races.

clue.text: Matching one in green with silver borders

indicators.note: borders means the silver symbol sits on either side of the rest

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: in puts the numeral one inside the colour word

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Two people match: one in green trimmed with silver.
explanation.walkthrough: AG splits, A at the front and G at the end, around GREEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing things correspond or tally with each other.

clue.text: Love the right to bargain for a tough business

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a deal is a bargain

explanation.surface: Bargaining over the right to love is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial or painful experience is a harrowing affair to go through.

clue.text: Taking exceptional care in public to appear excessively moved

indicators.note: taking means the public word holds the rearranged letters within it

parts.note: overt means open, done in public

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the letters of care in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Fussing in front of others so you look too emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERT takes in REAC, the letters of CARE reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond far more strongly than the situation warrants.

clue.text: Beast seen round those missing

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about and reordered

explanation.surface: A creature has been spotted near people who have gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Absentees are people not present.

clue.text: Wagers involving dope for dogs

indicators.note: involving means the wagers word wraps around the fool

parts.note: bets are wagers
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Bets on dogs that involve drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests doping racing dogs; it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassets are short-legged hounds.

clue.text: Combined to irritate a girl

parts.note: something that gets you annoys you
her refers to a woman or girl

explanation.surface: Joining forces to annoy a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done jointly are done in unison.

clue.text: Cattle feed by an Alpine lake

definitions.meaning: a fodder crop also called alfalfa

explanation.surface: Livestock graze beside a mountain lake in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both alfalfa grown for fodder and the Swiss city on its lake.

clue.text: The man, being aged, was not right internally

indicators.note: internally puts the rearranged letters inside the word for aged

parts.note: aged means old

indicators.note: not right says the letters of was are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: An old man was unwell inside.
explanation.walkthrough: SWA, the letters of WAS reworked, goes inside OLD. 'The man' defines a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswald is a male first name, so it can stand for a particular man.

clue.text: The old washerwoman's means of putting the squeeze on

definitions.text: The old washerwoman's means of putting the squeeze on

parts.words: The old washerwoman's means of putting the squeeze on
parts.note: suggests blackmail or pressure, but means the mangle that squeezed water out of wet laundry

explanation.surface: How a laundress of old exerted pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangle with rollers pressed water from washing before spin driers.

clue.text: Shelter provided if eels die unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters of eels die thrown into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Protection supplied if eels suddenly perish.
explanation.definitionFit: The side away from the wind gives protection, a sheltered side.

clue.text: Game may be let out when soldiers are around

indicators.note: are around means the soldiers surround the rearranged letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers

indicators.note: may be suggests let out can become another arrangement of those letters

explanation.surface: Play might be released when troops are near.
explanation.walkthrough: RE goes round OULETT, the letters of LET OUT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Trace about fifty, being smart

indicators.note: about puts the trace word around the Roman fifty

parts.note: a tinge is a trace or slight hint
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A hint of fifty, looking well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective (well dressed); it is the verb meaning sting.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting, a prickling sensation.

clue.text: Took the leavings

parts.note: reads as eating scraps, but leavings are what a person leaves in a will

explanation.surface: Someone who ate the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving property under a will means getting what the dead leave behind.

clue.text: The football team always carrying some weight

parts.note: ever means always
a ton is a measure of weight

explanation.surface: The team that is forever overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Liverpool football club in the English league.

clue.text: Given tea, grimace in disappointment

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
a grin is a facial expression, a grimace

explanation.surface: Served tea, someone pulls a face in disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or annoyance from failure.

clue.text: Set on after many break a leg

indicators.note: after puts on behind the letter for many

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

indicators.note: break signals the letters of a leg are smashed and reformed

explanation.surface: Theatrical good luck wish, issued after many performances.
explanation.walkthrough: GEAL is A LEG rearranged. 'Break a leg' is the actor's good luck phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To set is to solidify, as jelly firms up.

clue.text: Always unsophisticated, that's Rosemary!

parts.note: ever means always
green means naive, inexperienced

explanation.surface: Rosemary is forever naive.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary looks like a girl's name; it is the herb, a shrub that keeps its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a shrub that keeps its leaves all year, an example of this kind of plant.
